main.title: Doom: The Dark Ages
main.summary: Doom: The Dark Ages is a 2025 first-person shooter game developed by id Software and published by Bethesda Softworks.

cards.heading: The Slayer before the events of DOOM
cards.text: Doom: The Dark Ages is a 2025 first-person shooter game developed by id Software and published by Bethesda Softworks. It is the eighth main entry in the Doom franchise, following Doom Eternal (2020). A prequel to Doom (2016), it follows the Doom Slayer's efforts to combat a demonic invasion of the planet Argent D'Nur.

cards.heading: Development, release and Revelations
cards.text: id Software began work on Doom: The Dark Ages following the completion of Doom Eternal's post-launch campaign, The Ancient Gods, in 2021, entering full production by August 2022. The game was announced in June 2024, and was released on PlayStation 5, Windows, and Xbox Series X/S on May 15, 2025, to positive reviews from critics, who praised the game's combat systems and setting. An expansion pack, subtitled Revelations, was released on July 7, 2026.

main.title: Fast Fusion
main.subtitle: A new machine from two familiar ones
main.summary: Fast Fusion is Shin'en Multimedia's futuristic racing game, released with Nintendo Switch 2 on 5 June 2025.

cards.heading: A new machine from two familiar ones
cards.text: Fast Fusion is Shin'en Multimedia's futuristic racing game, released with Nintendo Switch 2 on 5 June 2025. The fourth Fast game continues the series' high-speed anti-gravity racing and colour-based phase switching. Its new fusion system combines vehicles into different machines, giving the player another way to shape a racing approach. Races reward placement with coins that purchase further cups, vehicles and combinations, linking performance on the circuit to the range of machines available for the next attempt.

cards.heading: Change phase and choose the next jump
cards.text: Coloured boost strips and jump pads require a matching vehicle phase. Changing colour at the right moment helps maintain speed and reach the intended route, while poorly timed switches interrupt that flow. Tracks demand attention to both the next bend and the coloured sections approaching it. Fusing two vehicles changes the machine brought to those situations, encouraging experiments with combinations rather than treating each unlocked craft as a fixed alternative. The race becomes the place where the practical difference between those choices can be felt.

cards.heading: Speed divides across a shared screen
cards.text: Local split-screen supports up to four players. Super Hero Mode increases the risk by using boost energy as health, forcing acceleration and survival to draw on the same reserve. Different performance options allow the presentation to balance resolution and visual detail, with support for HDR. Bjulin and Francisco Cerda contributed the music. Fast Fusion develops the series through its new hardware while keeping the central demand immediate: recognise the next piece of track, match its phase and preserve enough control to make the following decision.

main.title: Nintendo Switch 2
main.subtitle: The familiar hybrid, with a new set of inputs
main.summary: Nintendo Switch 2 keeps the hybrid console idea while changing how its controllers attach, move and connect players.

cards.heading: A larger window
cards.text: Nintendo Switch 2 keeps the portable screen and television dock at the centre of its design. Its larger 7.9-inch display gives that familiar arrangement more room, while the new dock supports higher-resolution output on a television.

cards.heading: Controllers that change roles
cards.text: Joy-Con 2 controllers attach magnetically and can also act as mouse-like pointing devices in supported software. A physical connection, a hand-held gesture and a movement across a table become different ways to control the same machine.

cards.heading: A collection that continues
cards.text: GameChat adds conversation and screen sharing to the system interface. Compatibility with much of the first Nintendo Switch library connects the new hardware to an existing collection rather than treating every generation as a clean break.
